title: Migrate per-request credits when adopting legacy EH Copilot CLI sessions
body:
Fixes  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/329999

### Summary

 When a legacy extension-host Copilot CLI session is migrated in place to the agent host, its per-request credit info was lost.

**Why it was lost:** the extension host persists credits in a sidecar file next to the SDK event log — `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/vscode.requests.metadata.json`, as `RequestDetails[]` with `creditsUsed`. The agent host instead keeps them in the per-session SQLite `turn_usage` table, which `AgentService._applyPersistedTurnUsage` overlays onto turns at restore. `mapSessionEvents` does not reconstruct usage from `events.jsonl`, so adoption — which reuses the event log verbatim and seeds only VS Code-layer metadata — left `turn_usage` empty.

**Fix:** after a successful adoption, `CopilotAgent._adoptLegacyTurnUsage` reads the sidecar and writes one `turn_usage` row per request. `RequestDetails.copilotRequestId` is the SDK `user.message` envelope id — the exact id `mapSessionEvents` restores turns under — so no id translation is needed. Credits convert to nano-AIU (`credits * 1e9`), the unit the renderer divides back out.

**Scope**

Deliberately limited to sessions actually being migrated. `_adoptLegacyTurnUsage` is called from exactly one place — the success path of `ensureChatAdopted`, past every eligibility gate — so it is unreachable for:

- native / already-adopted agent-host sessions (live usage stays authoritative, never rewritten)
- other Copilot SDK sessions sharing `~/.copilot` (standalone CLI, Local agent, the GitHub Copilot app's `origin: 'other'` markers)
- any session at all when `chat.agentSessions.migrateLegacyCopilotCli` is off (default)

No protocol, schema, or setting changes. The restore and live-usage paths are untouched.

title: Sessions are filtered out of the list in a remote window: working directories are compared without unwrapping their agent-host URIs
body:
### Summary

In a remote window (a dev container, here) agent sessions are filtered out of the sessions list because their working directories are reported as the remote's own `file:` URIs, while the workspace folder of such a window is a `vscode-remote:` URI. The containment check that decides list membership compares scheme first, so it can never match, however identical the paths are.

This is not a subset of sessions: in the `listSessions` payloads the agent host emitted in one log directory, **all 97 distinct sessions report `file:///workspace/printstream`, and none reports the `vscode-remote:` form**. So the list is empty in that window.

### Repro

1. Open a folder in a dev container.
2. Have agent sessions whose working directory is that folder.
3. Open the sessions list.

Observed: the sessions do not appear.

Expected: sessions on this workspace folder appear.

### Cause

List membership is decided by `_isSessionInWorkspace` → `_matchesAnyFolder` ([agentHostSessionListStore.ts:395-399](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostSessionListStore.ts#L395-L399)):

```ts
private _matchesAnyFolder(workingDirectories: readonly URI[], folders: readonly IWorkspaceFolder[]): boolean {
	return workingDirectories.some(directory =>
		folders.some(folder => extUriBiasedIgnorePathCase.isEqualOrParent(directory, folder.uri))
	);
}
```

`isEqualOrParent` gates on the scheme before it compares anything else ([resources.ts:171-176](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/base/common/resources.ts#L171-L176)):

```ts
isEqualOrParent(base: URI, parentCandidate: URI, ignoreFragment: boolean = false): boolean {
	if (base.scheme === parentCandidate.scheme) {
		...
	}
```

so a `file:` working directory against a `vscode-remote:` folder short-circuits to `false`.

Running that matcher against the two forms this host actually emits, with the real folder URI of the window:

```js
const folder   = URI.parse('vscode-remote://dev-container%2B7b22…/workspace/printstream');
const wdRemote = URI.parse('vscode-remote://dev-container%2B7b22…/workspace/printstream');
const wdFile   = URI.parse('file:///workspace/printstream');

extUriBiasedIgnorePathCase.isEqualOrParent(wdRemote, folder)  // true  -> would list
extUriBiasedIgnorePathCase.isEqualOrParent(wdFile,   folder)  // false -> filtered out
wdFile.path === folder.path                                   // true  -> only the namespace differs
```

### Both forms come from the same host

The session-list summaries carry the `file:` form:

```json
{"resource":"claude:/83d5b222-…","provider":"claude","title":"Grouped toasts for print jobs",
 "workingDirectories":["file:///workspace/printstream"]}
```

An opened session's state carries the `vscode-remote:` form instead — and mixes the two inside one payload, since `project.uri` stays `file:`:

```json
{"project":{"uri":"file:///workspace/printstream","displayName":"printstream"},
 "workingDirectories":["vscode-remote://dev-container%2B7b22…/workspace/printstream"]}
```

I have not established why the two paths differ, and I would rather report that than guess. The candidates I can see are that the URI recorded depends on how the session was created (one started from the workbench in a remote window is handed the `vscode-remote:` URI, one started inside the container records its own `file:` path), or that a translation is applied on the state path but not on the list path. Either way, the path that decides visibility is the one receiving untranslated URIs.

### Notes on fixing

I am not opening a PR with this, because the remedies I can see are design calls rather than something to guess at:

- normalize working directories into the client's namespace before they reach the list, keeping the comparison a strict URI containment check; or
- make the list comparison namespace-aware for remote windows.

Comparing on path alone does make the sessions appear, but I would not propose it: two different remotes exposing the same path would then compare equal.

### Environment

VS Code 1.133.0 (`a5b500951314efd502d07465bd138dfbd714a960`), Windows client, dev container remote, Claude provider, single-folder window.

- The agent can pick a model at creation that is not present on the agent host, causing the automation to fail to run later.

- Reported in internal discussion; appears related to how model pickers are populated by different chat input widgets and sessions. See related issue: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/330701

Fixes #329966
Fixes #329970

### Summary

Legacy Copilot CLI sessions that used a worktree didn't migrate when opened from the editor window, even though the same session migrated fine in the Agents window.

**Why:** the session list decides which sessions belong to your window by checking whether the session's folder sits inside the folder you have open. A worktree session runs in a separate folder *next to* the repository, not inside it — so it failed that check and never appeared in the list. Without it, clicking the session opened the old extension-host version instead of the agent-host one, and migration never ran. The Agents window has no folder open, so it shows everything and worked fine.

**Fix:** also match a session by its repository. The agent host already knows which repo a worktree session belongs to; that information just wasn't reaching the list. Now a session shows up if either its folder *or* its repository matches the window.

This only ever adds sessions to the list, never removes them, so nothing that shows today can disappear. Sessions from other repositories still don't appear.

It also fixes the same problem for regular (non-migrated) worktree sessions, which were invisible in folder windows too.

### Tests

Added a test covering a worktree session in a window opened on its repository, which also checks that a worktree from a *different* repository stays hidden.

title: Add regression tests for thenable RPC proxies
body:
Follow-up to #330923, which stopped the observable debugger RPC proxies and Copilot's worker RPC proxy from answering `then`. This adds the regression coverage that was intentionally left out of that PR.

## Why

Those proxies synthesize a callable for **any** property name, so without the guard `proxy.then` is a function and the proxy is a **thenable**. `await`ing one — or returning it from an `async` function — hands the promise machinery's own `resolve`/`reject` callbacks to a remote `then` call that never invokes them, and the await never settles. That is the deadlock originally hit in #330571.

The guards are four unremarkable-looking lines. Without tests, a future reader can delete them as dead code and silently reintroduce a hang that only shows up as a spinner in the UI.

## Tests

| Test | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `src/vs/base/test/common/observableInternal/logging/debugger/rpc.test.ts` | `SimpleTypedRpcConnection` `requests` + `notifications` proxies |
| `extensions/copilot/src/util/node/test/worker.spec.ts` | `createRpcProxy`, exposed publicly as `WorkerWithRpcProxy.proxy` |

Each asserts the proxy exposes no `then` and that awaiting it resolves to the proxy itself. The Copilot test additionally asserts no remote call was dispatched, since the failure mode is a spurious `then` call over the wire.

## Validation

Confirmed these are genuine regression tests, not tautologies — each was run with its corresponding guard temporarily reverted and **fails**, then passes once restored:

- Core, guards reverted: `AssertionError: + [AsyncFunction (anonymous)] - undefined`
- Copilot, guard reverted: fails on the `then` assertion
- Both green against current `main`

The core test needs `observableInternal` internals, so it carries an `eslint-disable-next-line local/code-no-deep-import-of-internal` matching the existing convention in `src/vs/base/test/common/observables/observable.test.ts`.

title: agentHost: stop legacy Copilot CLI sessions from migrating on list/scroll and enforce the migrate setting
body:
Fixes #330383

### Summary

**Context**
Two behaviors could still migrate extension-host Copilot CLI sessions the user never intended to migrate 

**1. Listing/scrolling migrated sessions.** The sessions list runs a read-state migration that dispatches session/isReadChanged for each row. In AgentService.dispatchAction, a session action on an un-loaded session triggers restoreSession → ensureChatAdopted, which writes the migration database. So merely refreshing or scrolling the list adopted sessions.

**2. Toggling the setting off didn't fully stop migration.** A session surfaced as adoptable while the setting was on stayed adoptable after it was turned off (migrateLegacyEnabled || surfacedAdoptable), so opening it still migrated — an ON→OFF inconsistency.

### **Changes (all in agentService.ts):**

**1. Passive read/archive actions no longer migrate.** Added _isPassiveMetadataAction and, in dispatchAction, drop a passive session/isReadChanged / isArchivedChanged action when it targets an un-loaded, surfaced-adoptable legacy session. The client applies read/archive optimistically and un-opened sessions hold no server-side pending state, so dropping the action is side-effect-free.

**2. Open-adoption strictly gated on the live setting.** In _doRestoreSession, adoption is now !external && migrateLegacyEnabled (removed the || surfacedAdoptable term). Migration happens only while the setting is on, and only on explicit open.

**3. Un-surface adoptable entries when the setting turns off.** Folded into the existing onDidRootConfigChange handler: on an ON→OFF transition, adoptable-legacy entries that were surfaced but never opened are retracted (reusing retractSurfacedSession; no data deleted). This removes the stale-entry dead-end that (2) would otherwise create — the extension-host provider entry takes back over, so the session stays visible and opens via the legacy path.

### **Behavior:**
**Setting OFF** (default): EH sessions remain visible; opening never migrates; listing/scrolling never migrates.
**Setting ON**: only an explicit open migrates; listing/scrolling/marking-read never does.
**ON → OFF** (same run): surfaced-but-unopened entries are retracted; opening no longer migrates; already-migrated sessions stay migrated.

### **Tests**
Updated the outdated "adopts even when the setting is off" test to the strict semantics (off → no adopt; on → adopts).
Added regressions for the passive-drop and the un-surface-on-disable behaviors.

### Setup

2. Enable `chat.omni.enabled` in your `settings.json`

4. For Voice Mode coverage, enable `agents.voice.enabled` and use a working microphone and speakers/headphones.

- Open Omni Chat from agents window. Verify it opens centered over the invoking window, receives keyboard focus, stays above the window, and does not replace or resize the main workbench.
- Drag the window using its leading grip. Verify dragging is reliable and does not activate Send or Close.

- Queue multiple prompts for a busy session. Verify each queued item retains its intended destination and accurately reports sent, cancelled, removed, or failed status.

### Questions, approvals, and routed results

title: sessions: collapse cloud sandboxes into one agent host filter entry
body:
## The problem

The agent host filter (the host picker on vscode.dev/agents) assumed **one provider = one host**. `AgentHostFilterService` turned every registered remote agent-host provider into exactly one picker entry, and `SessionsList.update()` scoped the list with `session.providerId === selectedProviderId`.

Cloud sandboxes broke that assumption. `CloudSandboxAgentHostContribution._ensureProvider` registers one provider **per sandbox environment** (`agenthost-cloudsandbox__<envId>`), and Mission Control creates one session per environment. So a user with 20 tasks got 20 picker entries, each showing exactly one session — burying the tunnel machines the picker exists to switch between.

The conceptual mismatch: a picker entry meant two things at once — *which machine am I connected to* (identity) and *which sessions do I see* (scope). For tunnels those are 1:1. A sandbox is a per-session ephemeral box, so the 1:1 assumption collapses.

Knock-on effects from the same root cause:
- Default selection could land on a sandbox — `_validate` fell back to `hosts[0]` sorted alphabetically, so a fresh vscode.dev profile could open scoped to a random task's ephemeral environment.
- `Manage Remote Agent Hosts…` listed every sandbox as a removable host.
- `WebWorkspacePicker` scoped new-session workspaces to a single entry, so "new session" targeted one sandbox.

Desktop was unaffected — `_applyHosts` only computes a selection when `isWeb`.

## The change

Decouple "connection" from "picker entry" via a new `IAgentHostGroup`. Each sandbox keeps its own provider and connection (one address, one credential set, one session-type authority), but providers sharing a group id fold into **one** filter entry.

- **`IAgentHostGroup`** (`sessions/common/agentHostSessionsProvider.ts`) — a provider may declare `hostGroup: { id, label, icon?, order?, connectable? }`. Tunnels/WSL/SSH omit it and keep the existing 1:1 mapping.
- **`IAgentHostFilterEntry`** gains `id`, `providerIds`, `icon`, and `connectable`. `AgentHostFilterService._rewatchProviders` buckets by `hostGroup?.id ?? provider.id` and rolls up member status (a group reads connected if any member is).
- **Selection is set-based** — `selectedProviderId` → `selectedHostId` + `selectedHost`. Consumers scope by the entry's whole `providerIds` set.
- **Cloud sandboxes declare the group** — `{ id: 'cloudsandbox', label: 'Cloud Sandboxes', icon: package, order: 1, connectable: false }`. `connectable: false` because a sandbox connects when one of its sessions is opened, so a connect/disconnect toggle would act on nothing the user pointed at.

Collateral fixes in the same change:
- `_validate` prefers the first **connectable** entry, so a fresh profile can't default into the sandbox group. (Worth noting: "Cloud Sandboxes" sorts before "Host A" alphabetically — only this rule keeps the default off it. There's a test for exactly this.)
- The connect/disconnect button is hidden and the "(disconnected)" menu suffix dropped for non-connectable entries — a group of 12 sandboxes reading "disconnected" looked broken.
- Grouped members are excluded from `Manage Remote Agent Hosts…` — you can't meaningfully "remove" a sandbox; discovery would just recreate it.
- `WebWorkspacePicker` shows recents across all group members but no "Select Folder…" for a group, since there's no single machine to browse.

## Migration

The persisted storage key is unchanged and now holds an entry id. A stale `agenthost-cloudsandbox__<envId>` value simply fails validation and falls through to the connectable-first fallback — no migration code needed.

## Reviewer notes

- **`_rewatchProviders` autorun**: `connectionStatus.read(reader)` is the unconditional first statement of every loop iteration, so no provider can drop out of the autorun's dependency set when grouping short-circuits.
- **Not done here**: the cleaner "one aggregate sandbox provider fanning out over N connections" refactor. Session ids, resource schemes, and chat content-provider registration are all derived per connection authority inside the 5.3k-line `BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider` — high risk, and not needed to fix this.

## Validation

- Typecheck clean (apart from two pre-existing errors in `assignmentService.ts`, a file this PR doesn't touch)
- ESLint clean, layers check clean, hygiene clean
- `agentHostFilterService.test.ts` — 12/12 pass, including 5 new tests covering folding, status rollup, `selectedHost.providerIds`, reconnect/disconnect fan-out, and the connectable-first fallback

**Still needs a CI run**: the browser-harness suites (`cloudSandboxAgentHostContribution.test.ts`, `tunnelAgentHost.contribution.test.ts`, sessionsList tests) import CSS/DOM and couldn't be driven from Node locally.

title: Add transient UI for /btw side questions
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

`/btw` currently opens another full chat. This change keeps the source transcript and composer in place and presents the side answer in a transient card immediately above the existing composer.

## Reviewer TL;DR

**A normal durable side chat, with a transient presentation.** The provider still owns the conversation, history, model and response. Closing removes only the card; the same backing chat remains recoverable from the session's Side Chats menu. **Open Full Chat** opens that conversation through the normal Sessions navigation path.

The feature defaults off behind `chat.agentSessions.transientSideChat` (`config.chat.agentSessions.transientSideChat` in ExP). Disabled treatment or an unavailable source host uses the existing full-chat open-and-split flow.

**Invariant:** `/btw` must not hide, replace, move, rebind, or restyle the source composer.

Rebased onto `main` at `17c5935aa72`. The history remains four dependency-ordered commits:

| Commit | Purpose | Review focus |
|---|---|---|
| `570205ea0fb` — `chat: refactor: support embedded response widgets` | Generic response-widget options, hidden-input layout, focus-local routing | Existing full-chat behavior stays the default; embedded renderers cannot shadow full surfaces |
| `41d2771964c` — `sessions: refactor: make send lifecycle explicit` | Request IDs, awaited `preserveActiveChat`, close history, provider option boundary | Concurrent and failing sends cannot affect another navigation follow |
| `2faa43c0465` — `sessions: feat: add transient side-chat presentation` | Card, rollout gate, orchestration, all entry points, accessibility and regressions | Presentation ownership, cleanup, error handling, focus and measured layout |
| `301fb9e55a9` — `agentHost: polish: skip side-chat rename round-trip` | Independent latency optimization | Rename reminder suppressed only for `SideChat` origins |

The durable architecture contract is in `src/vs/sessions/SESSIONS.md`, **Transient side questions**.

## Ownership and flow

```text
/btw, response-selection question, or workbench Ask in Side Chat
  -> create a real provider-backed side chat
  -> ISideChatOrchestrationService.prepare(...)
     -> control / no live interactive host: open and split the full side chat
     -> treatment + live host: close with skipHistory, publish transient state
  -> prepared.send(...)
     -> transient: awaited send with preserveActiveChat
     -> full: ordinary foreground send
  -> provider streams into the side-chat model
```

`ITransientSideChatService` stores resource identities, not provider facades. It resolves current session/chat state reactively and revalidates a per-source presentation ID after awaiting close. Replaced questions, deletion, facade replacement, setting disable, final-host disposal and read-only transitions cannot leave a stale live card.

`ISessionsManagementService` owns provider routing and paired send-start/send-end request IDs. `ISessionsService` owns visible navigation. The `background` and `preserveActiveChat` flags never cross the provider boundary; the explicit provider field picker has a compile-time exhaustiveness guard.

Promotion and full-chat fallback verify that the requested destination became active. A late promotion result cannot delete a replacement card.

## Layout and shared widget integration

The variable-height card is an **in-flow child of `ChatInputPart`**, after the floating status-pill lane and before banners/the original composer. It does not use the fixed-height floating lane or inherit that lane's pointer-event behavior.

The nested `ChatWidget` renders response rows only, with no header/footer, follow-ups, pet or go-to-bottom control, and no visible nested composer. It is created lazily; model loads are identity/cancellation guarded; dismissal releases the widget, model reference, listeners and scheduled layout.

`isEmbedded` provides focus-local action routing while excluding the renderer from full-widget discovery. Event-driven consumers use `lastFocusedChatSurface`. Embedded widgets inherit the enclosing surface's Find support, so Cmd/Ctrl+F continues working from the answer. Both Sessions and workbench Agent Host pills explicitly publish persistent-content visibility, including when the input is read-only.

Layout is frame-coalesced and skips unchanged dimensions. Short answers stay compact; long answers are capped at **60% of the source view**, including the fractional header height, divider and outer borders. Scrolling remains inside the answer. Auto routing metadata is hidden only inside transient cards; the ordinary full chat still shows it.

## Failure handling and accessibility

`FailedAndPresented` means a live card owns the send failure. Dismissed or promoting cards decline that ownership, allowing normal caller notification instead of losing the error during promotion. Failure details are retained if promotion itself fails.

The card is a labelled region described by its question and visible status. Announcements are transition-based. Escape dismisses a pending or completed card, but yields to code-editor selections, suggestion UI and hover. From the source input it additionally yields to active requests, dictation, editing and confirmation interactions. Close returns source focus; successful promotion focuses the full-chat destination.

## Review and verification

Opus 5 maximum-reasoning reviews covered Sessions presentation, lifecycle/orchestration, shared workbench behavior and latest-main integration. Findings were fixed and re-reviewed. The OSS run then exposed routing metadata and border-budget regressions; those were fixed, regression-covered, re-reviewed, and the entire live flow was repeated.

Current validation:

- Complete development build via `npm run build-fast`; client type check and changed-file ESLint/Stylelint pass.
- **283 focused Electron tests pass** (2 existing pending), including send/promotion races, read-only pill visibility, real fractional-header/border measurement, metadata scoping, source input, Find and side-chat entry points.
- **44 Agent Host title tests pass**.
- **Ten authenticated, provider-backed Code OSS scenarios pass on the final rebased build**: source context/composer identity and styling; Find from the card; draft preservation; strict height cap; internal wheel scrolling; code-selection Escape; promotion; pending-card dismissal; selected-response questions; and live setting disable/full-chat fallback.
- Measured long-answer geometry: **524.40625px card in an 876px source view**, below the **525.6px cap**, with **1,410px** scroll extent in a **467px** response viewport.

Screenshots, a Playwright trace, assertion results and a 59-second recording were retained with the session's OSS evidence report.

## Context

`Ctrl/Cmd+F` opens a Find widget over the chat transcript. It is available in the Chat view, chat editors, and the Agents Window chat pane, and searches the whole conversation rather than only what is currently on screen.

Two behaviours are intentional and should **not** be reported as bugs:

- Text inside **tool pills** (for example a terminal command header) is not searchable.
- Text inside **collapsed reasoning** ("thinking") is not searchable.

Both are excluded because Find cannot reliably scroll to and highlight them, so counting them would produce results that go nowhere.

## Test Steps

1. Open a chat with a reasonably long conversation and press `Ctrl/Cmd+F`
   - The Find widget should appear over the transcript with the input focused
   - Repeat in each host: the Chat view, a chat editor (`Chat: Open in Editor`), and the Agents Window chat pane
   - Press `Ctrl/Cmd+F` with focus in the composer, and again with focus inside a rendered code block — both should open the same Find widget
   - Open Quick Chat and inline chat and confirm `Ctrl/Cmd+F` does **not** open the chat Find widget there
2. Type a word that appears several times in the conversation
   - The widget should show a match count, and matches should be highlighted
   - The current match should be visually distinct from the other matches
   - Navigate with `Enter` / `Shift+Enter`, `F3` / `Shift+F3`, and the up/down buttons in the widget
   - Every step should move the view to the match it lands on, and navigation should wrap at the ends
3. Search for a word that appears near the very beginning of a long conversation, then navigate to it
   - The transcript should scroll to the match even though it was far off screen
   - If the match is inside a collapsed **Completed N steps** disclosure, the disclosure should expand and reveal it
4. Search for a word that appears deep inside a long code block in a response
   - The code block should scroll to the match and highlight it there
5. Try the **Match Case**, **Whole Word**, and **Regular Expression** toggles
   - Results should change accordingly
   - With regex enabled, type an invalid expression (for example `([`) — the widget should show no results without throwing an error
6. Open Find while a response is still streaming and search for a word the model is actively writing
   - New matches should be picked up as the response grows
   - Navigation should keep working while content arrives
7. Open two chats side by side (split chat editors, or two Agents Window panes) and open Find in both
   - Each widget should keep its own search text, match count, and highlights
   - `F3` should act on the chat that currently has focus, not the other one

title: Notebook edits by Copilot agent spawn multiple untitled notebook duplicates
body:
### Version

- VS Code: 1.132.0 (df53daabb18cd157bdb08c7f01c34df936cf12f4, x64)
- OS: Windows
- ms-toolsai.jupyter: 2025.9.1

### Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?

Not tested — the Jupyter extension is required to reproduce.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a workspace containing a `.ipynb` file.
2. Ask Copilot (agent mode) to make edits to that notebook, over several turns.
3. Observe new dirty `Untitled-N.ipynb` editors appearing after edit rounds.

### Expected

Edits apply to the target notebook only. No additional untitled notebook documents are created.

### Actual

Each edit round spawns one or more dirty `Untitled-N.ipynb` editors that are full duplicates of the notebook being edited. They persist as backups under `%APPDATA%\Code\Backups\<hash>\untitled\` and are restored on subsequent window startups.

### Evidence

Observed on two consecutive days with the same signature.

**Day 1** — real file `39,831 B`, modified 21:39:14:

| Document | Backup written | Size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Untitled-1.ipynb | 21:38:56 | 40,161 B |
| Untitled-2.ipynb | 21:39:42 | 40,161 B |
| Untitled-3.ipynb | 21:39:55 | 40,161 B |

**Day 2** — real file `42,594 B`:

| Document | Backup written | Size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Untitled-2 | 19:55:49 | 42,809 B |
| Untitled-3 | 19:55:56 | 42,809 B |
| Untitled-6 | 19:56:08 | 42,809 B |
| Untitled-7 | 19:56:19 | 42,809 B |
| Untitled-1 | 19:57:42 | 42,809 B |
| Untitled-4 | 20:19:26 | 42,809 B |

Verified by parsing the backup payload against the on-disk notebook:

- Identical cell count (13 vs 13)
- First cell source matches byte-for-byte
- Untitled sizes track the real file's growth across days (32,248 → 40,161 → 42,809), confirming they mirror the edited notebook

### Additional notes

- The backup directory hash has **no corresponding `workspaceStorage` entry**, i.e. the untitled documents are bucketed against an *empty window*, not the open workspace.
- Gaps in the numbering (`Untitled-5` absent; 6 and 7 present) indicate more copies are created than are persisted — some are closed before the backup flush.
- `"files.hotExit": "off"` stops them surviving a restart but does **not** prevent creation.
- No duplicate notebook extensions installed; no OneDrive conflict copies on disk.
- Deleting the backup files while the editors are open is ineffective — VS Code rewrites them on the next flush.

Users should not have to specify full paths when asking an agent to work in a project already known to VS Code agent sessions.

## Proposed behavior

Improve the existing `list_sessions` and `create_session` tools so they preserve and resolve complete workspace information without adding another model-visible tool.

`list_sessions` should:

- return the configured project URI while preserving the project display name
- return additional working directories for multi-root sessions while preserving the primary working directory
- filter by project display name, project URI, or any working directory

`create_session` should:

- continue accepting absolute paths, workspace URIs, and known working directories
- accept a unique project display name and resolve it to the configured project root
- report candidate project URIs when a display name is ambiguous
- accept remote/non-file project URIs

This supports natural-language requests such as “run this in the vscode workspace” while avoiding an additional always-advertised tool and avoiding accidental reuse of a transient worktree.

## Acceptance criteria

- Agents can discover configured project roots through known sessions.
- Multi-root sessions expose every working directory.
- A unique project display name can be passed directly to session creation.
- Ambiguous names do not silently select a workspace.
- Returned local or remote URIs can be passed directly to session creation.
- Existing `project` and `workingDirectory` fields remain compatible.
- Workspace matching uses URI comparison semantics.

A global recent-workspace catalog, usage-frequency ranking, fuzzy natural-language resolution, and new-folder permission flows are intentionally out of scope.

title: Plugins tab: remote-plugin rows have no component fixture coverage, hiding shared-CSS regressions
body:
## Gap

`PluginRemoteItemRenderer` in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/pluginListWidget.ts` renders five distinct status states as **text**:

| State | String |
|---|---|
| disabled | `Disabled` |
| loading | `Loading` |
| loaded | `Loaded` |
| degraded | `Warning` |
| error | `Error` |

None of them is covered by a component fixture. The AI Customizations editor has ten plugin fixtures (`PluginsTab`, `PluginsTabScrolled`, `PluginBrowseMode`, `PluginDetail`, `PluginsDisabledByUser`, …) and not one exercises a remote-plugin row, so this renderer has no screenshot coverage at all.

## Why it matters — this already hid a real bug

Both plugin renderers deliberately reuse the MCP row styling (`// Installed Plugin Renderer (reuses .mcp-server-item CSS)`), including `.mcp-server-status`. That rule was sized for a codicon glyph:

```css
.mcp-server-item .mcp-server-status {
    width: var(--vscode-spacing-size240);   /* 24px */
    height: var(--vscode-spacing-size240);
    justify-content: center;
    font-size: var(--vscode-codiconFontSize);
}
```

So the five text labels above were being rendered into a fixed 24×24 box. It went unnoticed because nothing renders those rows in CI.

The styling side is fixed as a side-effect of #330943, which reshapes that rule to be text-shaped. The **coverage** gap remains: the next change to shared `.mcp-server-item` styling has the same blind spot, and a reviewer looking at screenshot diffs will again see no movement for this renderer whether or not it is broken.

## Suggested fix

Add a fixture exercising `PluginRemoteItemRenderer` across its status states — a remote-agent-host plugin list with rows in `loading` / `loaded` / `degraded` / `error` / disabled. That makes the shared-CSS coupling between the MCP and Plugins tabs visible in screenshot diffs, which is the property that was missing.

## Notes

Found while reviewing the shared-CSS blast radius of #330943. Not filed there because it is a Plugins-tab coverage gap rather than part of that change.

| #330207 | `main` today, used here |
|---|---|
| `get/setMcpServerEnablement`, keyed by server **name** | `setCustomizationEnablement(...)`, keyed by customization **id** |
| `resolveMcpDisabledState`, `formatMcpStatusWithScope`, `getStatusScopeNote`, `McpEnablementScope` | `getCustomizationDisabledLabel` + `CustomizationDisabledReason` — which also knows `Disabled (Plugin)` |
| `IAgentHostDurableEnablement` | deleted |
| `mcpServerIdentity.ts` | already inlined in `mcpListWidget.ts` |

## What changes

**Status became legible.** `getMcpStatusPresentation` returned no icon for `Stopped`, and the render path bailed out on a missing icon — so the most common row in the list drew *zero pixels*, and the rows that did draw asked you to infer meaning from a colour. Status is now a word beside the name with a colour dot, shown only when it adds something: `Failed`, `Sign-in needed`, `Starting`, scope-qualified `Disabled (…)`. `Running`/`Idle` are suppressed (MCP servers start lazily; liveness is noise), and a bare `Disabled` is suppressed on a row whose switch already says it. The **accessible name deliberately keeps** the plain `Disabled` — a screen reader reads the row label without the switch beside it.

**Every row that can be turned off has a switch.** Previously right-click only. Failing rows get a labelled **Show Output** button instead of a coloured icon that was both the only sign of failure and the only way to read why.

**Rows say what a server offers.** Tool counts read from cache state, so they survive an idle server. Line two is *origin · transport · (error **or** description)*.

**Four sections by origin** — User, Workspace, Extensions & Plugins, Built-in — with agent-contributed servers folded into Built-in, naming their product on the row.

**The detail pane is worth opening**: full tool list with descriptions, plus the command/address. Env-var and header **values are never rendered, only names** — they routinely carry tokens.

## The switch's write semantics

The decisive decision is `enablement[0]`, so the switch replaces **that kind** — this is what actually moves the effective state, and it answers a deliberate workspace or session choice where it was made instead of silently promoting it. With nothing decided yet it writes **Global**: an unqualified control means the whole durable answer.

Deliberately **not** `IAgentHostMcpServer.setEnabled`, which only writes the session layer. Reads and writes are **live**, because the render guard cannot cover every decision in an enablement array and writing back a captured one would resurrect a scope the user had since changed.

Local enablement is keyed by the **workbench server id** — the key `EnableMcpServerGloballyAction` already uses — not the matched runtime `definition.id`. That match is deliberately conservative and declines whenever two servers share a name; a row must not lose its switch, or misreport its status, over an ambiguity in a lookup it never needed.

### Two deliberate exceptions (please read as intent, not oversight)

- **A gallery result gets no switch** — nothing is installed to turn on.
- **A server disabled by its owning plugin gets no switch.** Writing its own enablement cannot free it, so it keeps the word `Disabled (Plugin)` and the context menu's **Enable {plugin}** rather than a control that would appear to do nothing.

Both were confirmed with the requester before implementation.

### Known limitation

`withCustomizationEnablement` replaces one kind at a time, so a server held off at **both** Global and Session cannot be turned "on everywhere" in a single gesture. Writing the deciding kind always moves the *effective* state, but a broader `false` survives and re-asserts later (e.g. in a new session). This matches the context menu's own per-scope semantics — silently deleting a broader durable choice would be worse. Documented in `AI_CUSTOMIZATIONS.md`.

## Note for the #330890 reviewer

This **widens `IMcpStatusRenderInput`** (adds `switchChecked`, `errorMessage`, `toolCount`, `toolsFromCache`, `transport`, `description`, `origin`, `impliedOrigin`; removes `statusIconId` along with the icon it described).

That is a consequence of the design, not an oversight: line two draws on `transport` and `errorMessage`, which are only known once the row's observables have been read, so it genuinely cannot be built in `renderElement` any more. The failure mode is silent — a field left out doesn't throw, it freezes that text on screen until something else happens to move — so the mapped-type test was left to drive every addition. It caught me twice.

The guard is also now fed the **live** agent-host server rather than the entry's snapshot. `logOutputChannelId` and the scoped id are pure derivations of the session and customization id, so the signature still only moves when the server is genuinely republished — and it fixes an output action that could stay bound to a dead channel.

## This PR also changes the Plugins tab

Not obvious from the title, so stating it plainly. `pluginListWidget.ts` reuses this tab's row CSS — `// Installed Plugin Renderer (reuses .mcp-server-item CSS)` — and both of its renderers add `.mcp-server-item`. Two shared rules changed:

**`.mcp-server-item.disabled`** — was a blanket `opacity: 0.5` on the whole row. It now dims only the name and description, so a disabled row's status and error text stay readable (they are the reason you are looking at the row). Both plugin renderers set `.disabled`, so **the "Disabled Locally" group on the Plugins tab dims slightly differently**. Expect `PluginsTab` / `PluginsTabScrolled` baselines to move a little.

**`.mcp-server-status`** — was a fixed `24×24` box with `justify-content: center` and `font-size: var(--vscode-codiconFontSize)`, i.e. sized for a codicon glyph. But `PluginRemoteItemRenderer` writes **text** into it (`"Loading"`, `"Loaded"`, `"Warning"`, `"Error"`, `"Disabled"`), so remote-plugin status has been clipping into a 24px box. My text-shaped rule fixes that.

That second one is **a fix, not a side-effect** — but no baseline will show it, because no fixture exercises the remote-plugin renderer. Flagging it so "shared rule changed, nothing moved" doesn't read as suspicious. It is visible only against a remote agent host.

## Reactivity

`getMcpServers` is a plain read, so a `derived` over it never re-runs. `ActiveSessionMcpServerReader` folds it into the reactive graph via `observableSignalFromEvent(onDidChangeCustomizations)`. Aria labels are `IObservable<string>` because a row's status changes without the list being spliced.

Session servers are claimed against the **unfiltered** lists and filtered afterwards — `take` is consuming, so a row hidden by the search box would otherwise release its claim. The sidebar badge is computed the same way; it previously grew while you typed.

The detail pane does **not** re-derive the join: the matcher is consuming and order-dependent, so a fresh match there can adopt a server the list already gave to another row. The row's claim travels with the selection.

## Validation

- `tsc --project src/tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean — and **each of the 10 commits typechecks standalone** (verified in an isolated worktree)
- 39 `mcpListWidget` + 4 `enablement` + 8 agent-host MCP tests passing
- eslint + stylelint clean
- 82 component fixtures rendered and visually reviewed; adds a scrolled active-session fixture, since Built-in is where agent servers land and no screenshot could reach it
- The fixtures gained a working enablement model — the stub they had rendered every server as off, and failed silently because the read happens inside an autorun

title: Anchor branch changes on the session baseline checkpoint
body:
Fixes #330941.

### Problem

Branch Changes are diffed against `merge-base HEAD origin/<base>`, which assumes a session owns its branch. A session started on an existing long-lived branch reports that branch's entire divergence instead of its own work: every session in the repository shows the same number, it grows with each commit whether or not a session touched anything, and a session that edited two files can read as sixteen thousand insertions.

Measured on a real repository: `104 files changed, 11448 insertions(+), 1285 deletions(-)` against a session that touched two files, purely because its branch was ahead of `main`.

### Fix

Anchor the diff on the session's baseline checkpoint when one exists. The host already captures that checkpoint once per session per repository, so it is exactly "the state when this session started", and the diff becomes the session's footprint.

A session that owns its branch is unaffected: its baseline is the branch point, so the number is unchanged. Without a baseline (checkpoints unavailable, non-git folder, capture failed) the base branch is still used.

The anchor is resolved in one place and used by both the primary and per-repository diffs, so the branch changeset, the session-list chip, and every path that derives the chip from that changeset stay consistent. That consistency is the reason this changes the changeset rather than only the chip: `computeListEntryChanges` re-derives the chip from the branch changeset on cold paths and persists what it derives, so anchoring only the summary makes the number flip between two definitions across an active/inactive transition.

No extra git diff is introduced; the anchor replaces the base on the existing call. Resolving it costs one `rev-parse` per repository per recompute.

### Scope, and what to push back on

This changes what the Branch Changes view shows for a session on a shared branch: the session's changes rather than the branch's. For a branch-owning session nothing changes. Commit and pull-request flows are untouched, since both call `computeSessionFileDiffs` directly with the base branch rather than reading the changeset ([pull request handler](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostPullRequestOperationHandler.ts#L164), [commit handler](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostCommitOperationHandler.ts#L93)).

If the branch-wide definition is deliberate for that view, the alternative is to keep it and give the list its own session-scoped count, which is a larger change to the summary plumbing.

### Verification

Two tests: a session with a baseline reports only its own changes rather than the branch divergence, and a session without one falls back to the base branch. 5296 agent host tests pass; the 3 failures are present on `main` unchanged.

title: Session list change counts show the whole branch divergence, not the session's changes
body:
> **Update:** struck-through passages below are corrections to my original report — two measurements came from the wrong repository, and the suggested fix turned out to be wrong. Details, re-measured figures and further evidence in [this comment](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/330941#issuecomment-5299050850). The report itself stands.

### Summary

The change counts shown against a session in the sessions list are the whole branch's divergence from its base branch, not that session's changes. On a long-lived shared branch the number grows without bound, is identical for every session in the repository, and wildly overstates what an agent did.

### Repro

1. Work on a branch that is well ahead of the default branch (a long-lived `dev`, say).
2. Start a session there and let it edit one or two files.
3. Look at the session in the sessions list.

Observed: a count in the thousands, close to identical for every session in that repository, growing over time.

Expected: what this session changed.

### Cause

The list chip renders `changes.insertions/deletions` ([agentSessionsViewer.ts:542](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentSessionsViewer.ts#L542)), sourced from the Branch changeset summary ([agentHostChangesetService.ts:1356](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostChangesetService.ts#L1356)), which is `git diff` against `merge-base HEAD origin/<base>` ([agentHostGitService.ts:474](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostGitService.ts#L474)).

That is correct when a session owns its branch, which is the cloud/PR shape. For a local session started on an existing shared branch, the merge-base is far behind and the diff is dominated by work no session performed.

~~Measured on a real repository: a session that touched two files sat on a `dev` branch whose `git diff --shortstat $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)` was `104 files changed, 11448 insertions(+), 1285 deletions(-)`. A second repository whose branch was level with its remote correctly showed only its uncommitted `209 insertions, 6 deletions`, which is the same code path behaving differently purely because of branch position.~~

**Corrected.** Both figures above were misreported: the first came from a different repository than the screenshot, and the second was not a second repository at all. Re-measured on the repository this report came from, on its `dev` branch:

```
$ git diff --shortstat $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)
 166 files changed, 11329 insertions(+), 634 deletions(-)

$ git ls-files --others --exclude-standard | wc -l    # 17 untracked files,
 17                                                    # totalling 4741 lines

$ git diff --shortstat origin/dev                      # same repo, own remote
 9 files changed, 209 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)    # HEAD level with origin/dev
```

`166 + 17 = 183` files and `11329 + 4741 = 16070` insertions is exactly what the chip displays (`183 files, +16070 -634`); the branch changeset includes untracked files, `--shortstat` alone does not. The `209 insertions, 6 deletions` is the *same* repository measured against its own remote branch rather than the default branch — which still makes the original point, and makes it on one repository: the identical code path reports `11329` or `209` purely according to which base it resolves.

### Suggested fix

~~The host already captures a per-session baseline checkpoint per repository (`IAgentHostCheckpointService.captureBaselineCheckpoint`, retrievable via `getBaselineCheckpoint`). Anchoring the branch diff there makes the number the session's own footprint, and leaves a branch-owning session unchanged because its baseline is the branch point.~~

~~PR follows. Happy to close it if the current definition is deliberate, in which case the counts may still be worth relabelling, since as displayed they read as the session's work.~~

**Withdrawn.** That was tried in #330942 and closed: a baseline checkpoint is a parentless snapshot commit rather than an ancestor of `HEAD`, so it cannot be used as the base of a merge-base working-tree diff — doing so compared unrelated trees and produced a worse number than the one it replaced.

No new computation is needed in any case. The `session` changeset already diffs the session's baseline checkpoint against its latest turn checkpoint via the two-ref primitive ([agentHostChangesetService.ts:1541-1566](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostChangesetService.ts#L1541-L1566)), which is the session's own footprint. The open question is only which changeset feeds the chip — and that is a product decision, since the branch-derived chip is deliberate (#323852, pinned by a characterization test). The counts may still be worth relabelling, since as displayed they read as the session's work.

title: Fix Explorer case-sensitivity validation by probing capabilities in FileService
body:
Fixes #94307

**The Problem:**
On mixed-case operating systems like macOS (where APFS volumes can be optionally case-sensitive), the Explorer was incorrectly rejecting files with differing cases (e.g., `test.txt` and `TEST.TXT`) even on case-sensitive volumes. 

The validation logic relied on `ExplorerModel.fetchChildren` to prime the `PathCaseSensitive` capability cache. However, during workspace restore on startup, folders are resolved in bulk and pre-populated (`isDirectoryResolved = true`), which caused the capability probing in `fetchChildren` to be completely bypassed. This resulted in cache misses during validation and an incorrect fallback to case-insensitive assumptions.

Furthermore, the `DiskFileSystemProvider` wrapper in `electron-browser` lacked the `isPathCaseSensitive` delegate method, meaning any attempt to query the provider evaluated to `undefined` and fell back to static capabilities.

**The Solution:**
1. **Architectural fix:** Moved the cache-priming logic entirely out of the UI (`ExplorerModel`) and into the core `FileService.resolve()`. Now, anytime a directory is resolved by the core engine, its case-sensitivity is asynchronously queried and cached at the scheme-root level. This guarantees the cache is primed regardless of how the UI restores its state.
2. **Plumbing fix:** Plumbed `isPathCaseSensitive(resource: URI): Promise<boolean>` through the `DiskFileSystemProvider` wrapper in `electron-browser` so it properly delegates to the underlying `DiskFileSystemProviderClient`.
3. **Performance:** `FileService` now utilizes a `TernarySearchTree` to map case sensitivity capabilities at the root level, avoiding expensive redundant disk I/O on deep directory traversals.

**How to Test:**
1. Create a case-sensitive volume on macOS.
2. Open a folder on that volume in VS Code.
3. Create `test.txt`.
4. Attempt to create `TEST.TXT`. It should successfully create the file.

title: Proposal: execute a client tool on the runtime's invocation
body:
**Proposal, and easy to decline.** #330899 asks whether the stream-mapper ready is meant to be actionable. This is what the alternative looks like, offered so the option is concrete rather than hypothetical. If the current ordering is deliberate, closing this costs nothing and the three symptom PRs still stand on their own.

Stacked on #330746, which introduces the `client_tool_invoked` signal this builds on.

### The seam

A client tool is executed when its streamed tool call reaches `Running` ([agentSideEffects.ts:566-575](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentSideEffects.ts#L566-L575)), in parallel with the runtime invoking the same tool through its in-process MCP server. The MCP handler discards its arguments and parks, so the streamed ready is the active trigger and the invocation is a passive await.

Three defects follow from that one trigger:

| Defect | Why the trigger allows it | PR |
|---|---|---|
| The tool runs twice | The ready fires from the stream mapper and again from the permission flow | #330683 |
| The tool runs with `{}` | A synthesized ready carries no `toolInput` | #330684 |
| The result is dropped | Execution can finish before the SDK registers the handler that awaits it | #330730 |

### The change

A provider may declare `drivesClientToolExecution`, meaning its runtime reports every client tool invocation. For those providers the host admits a call to execution only once the invocation arrives, rather than on the streamed ready. Claude opts in, since its in-process MCP server sees every call the SDK makes. Providers with no such signal are untouched, so Copilot and Codex keep executing on `Running`.

Because the invocation carries the runtime's own arguments, a streamed call that arrived without input is repaired from them before it runs.

All three defects then become structurally impossible for Claude rather than individually patched: one trigger instead of two, real arguments instead of `{}`, and `registerAndFire` ordering registration before execution.

### What this costs

Execution starts at the SDK round trip rather than when the arguments finish streaming. If that latency is the reason the ready is actionable today, this is the wrong trade and I would rather know than guess. That is the question in #330899.

### Verification

New test: with a provider that announces invocations, a streamed ready produces no execution request and the invocation does. 5298 agent host tests pass; the 3 failures are present on `main` unchanged.

﻿## Summary

Prevents the Agent Host signed-out models notification from appearing during startup for users who are already signed in to GitHub Copilot.

## Root cause

`AgentHostSignedOutModelsNotificationContribution` waited for the default-account service, but default-account and chat-entitlement initialization are independent. During startup, `currentDefaultAccount` can resolve to `null` while the chat entitlement is still `Unresolved`. Once model readiness settled, the contribution interpreted that state as signed out and published the "Choose how you want to use Copilot" notification.

The Copilot extension could then resolve the entitlement to a signed-in plan and make chat fully usable. The contribution did not listen to `onDidChangeEntitlement`, so the stale notification remained even though Copilot chat worked and the Accounts menu showed the signed-in account.

This change:

- keeps the notification hidden until chat entitlement resolves;
- treats any resolved entitlement other than `Unknown` as signed in, while retaining the default-account snapshot as an early signed-in signal;
- re-evaluates the notification when entitlement changes;
- covers both `Unresolved -> Pro` and genuine `Unresolved -> Unknown` startup transitions.

Fixes the Automations custom view failing to open. When the view ID moved to a neutral constants module, nothing imported `automationsView.ts` anymore, so its module-level `registerWorkbenchContribution2(...)` never ran and the view was never registered.

title: Guard RPC proxies against becoming thenables
body:
## Problem

#330569 fixed `ProxyChannel.toService`, whose `get` trap answered **every** string property with a function — including `then`. That made the proxy a **thenable**: `await`ing it, or returning it from an `async` function, handed the promise machinery's own `resolve`/`reject` callbacks to a remote `then` call that never invoked them, so the awaiting promise stayed pending forever.

That root cause is not unique to `ProxyChannel`. Auditing every `new Proxy` site in the repo turned up three more proxies that synthesize a callable for **any** property name, so `proxy.then` is always a function and each is a latent deadlock of exactly the same shape.

## Fix

Stop answering `then` in each, matching the existing guards in [`ipc.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/base/parts/ipc/common/ipc.ts), [`editor.worker.start.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/editor/editor.worker.start.ts) and [`standaloneWebWorker.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/editor/standalone/browser/standaloneWebWorker.ts):

| Proxy | Consequence without the guard |
| --- | --- |
| Observable debugger RPC `requests` | `await` dispatches a bogus RPC request named `then` |
| Observable debugger RPC `notifications` | `await` dispatches a bogus notification named `then` |
| Copilot `createRpcProxy` | `await` calls the worker with non-cloneable promise callbacks |
| Copilot parser timeout proxy | Needs its **own** guard — it wraps the worker proxy, so fixing `createRpcProxy` alone leaves the outer proxy thenable |

Each guard carries a one-line comment, since a bare `if (prop === 'then') return undefined;` reads as dead code and could be removed later, silently reintroducing the hang.

## Notes

- The mirrored copy under `extensions/copilot/src/util/vs/**` is deliberately untouched: that tree is marked read-only and synced from the canonical `microsoft/vscode` sources, so the fix belongs in `src/vs/base/...` and will propagate on the next sync.
- Wrapper proxies built on `Reflect.get` (e.g. `extHostConfiguration`, `taggedCacheInterceptor`, `playwrightService`) are **not** affected — they inherit their target's thenability rather than fabricating `then`. Likewise the `$`-prefixed RPC proxies in `rpcProtocol.ts` and `webWorker.ts` only synthesize known method shapes.
- These are latent hazards hardened preventatively; I did not find a second user-visible hang beyond the one #330569 already fixed.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` — clean
- Copilot `tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json` — clean
- Verified locally with regression tests asserting `proxy.then === undefined` and that `await Promise.resolve(proxy) === proxy` for both the debugger RPC and worker RPC proxies (kept out of this PR by request).

Follow-up from the scoped-enablement work (#330566, #330715).

## Problem

Three separate times during that work, a validation run **looked green while having verified nothing**:

1. **Stale `out/`** — the Electron unit runner exited `0` having run no tests, because a merge left a stale compiled module and the runner died on an unrelated dynamic-import error. Fixed by `npm run transpile-client`.
2. **Zero-match grep selector** — `./scripts/test.sh --grep "customizationEnablement"` matched **no tests** and reported success-shaped output. The suites are capitalized (`CustomizationEnablement`), and the real selector runs 35 tests. Three separate agents reported `0 passing` before anyone noticed the selector was wrong.
3. **Policy checks reading as build failures** — `VS Code Merge Check` / `⭐️ VS Code` reported `fail`, but the check-run output title was `Skipped due to merge conflicts`: the build never ran. Easy to misread as a real regression and go hunting for a nonexistent bug.

A small `scripts/validate-agent-host.sh` (or npm script) that runs the standard agent-host validation set and **asserts a minimum test count** for each command, failing loudly when a run reports fewer tests than expected. That turns "suspiciously small summary" from something a human has to notice into a hard failure.

# 2 pre-existing errors in src/vs/workbench/services/assignment/common/assignmentService.ts are expected

./scripts/test.sh --grep "CustomizationEnablement|McpCustomizationController|Codex"   # 225 passing

title: agent host: stop deleting enablement decisions against a mutable client base

labels.name: debt
labels.description: Code quality issues

labels.name: agent-host
labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

body:
Follow-up cleanup from the scoped-enablement work (#330566, #330715).

## Problem

The overlay model in `AgentHostCustomizationEnablementService` is correct but is the subtlest thing in the subsystem, and its failure mode was a **write that silently erased itself**.

The model: the client's global value is the *base*, host decisions layer on top, and "store only what differs" compares against that base rather than a hardcoded default. `_setPersistentDecision` deletes a decision that matches its inherited value, so the UI can restore inheritance without a third "Inherit" action.

The bug it produced: `replaceEnablement` wrote a decision, which synchronously triggered a republish, which fed the client's *stale* global back in, which made the just-written decision look redundant, which deleted it. The user's disable silently did nothing. Diagnosing it required a call stack showing the loop.

The residual hazard is that the comparison base is **mutable and asynchronous**. `_clientGlobalEnablement` can change after a host decision is stored, at which point a previously-stored decision may become "redundant" — or, worse, a decision that should exist was never stored because it matched a base that has since changed.

## Suggestion

Stop using the client global as a *deletion trigger*. Always persist explicit host decisions, and use the client global purely as the inheritance root when resolving. Deletion then happens only on an explicit user action (clear/reset), never as a side effect of a base value moving.

Cost is a few more stored entries. Storage was never the constraint — there is already a 512-entry LRU with eviction — and the reduction in reasoning burden is significant: the invariant becomes "we store what the user told us" rather than "we store what differs from a value that can change underneath us."

## Guard

Keep the regression coverage around `replaceEnablement` → republish → `applyClientGlobalEnablement`, which is where the self-defeating write happened.

title: agent host: one representation and one cascade rule for customization enablement

labels.name: debt
labels.description: Code quality issues

labels.name: agent-host
labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

body:
Follow-up cleanup from the scoped-enablement work (#330566, #330715).

## Problem

There are three representations of "is this on?" in session state:

- `DirectoryCustomization.enabled: boolean` (`state.ts:861`)
- `ChildCustomizationBase.enabled?: boolean` (`state.ts:894`)
- `enablement?: CustomizationEnablement[]` on `PluginCustomization` and `McpServerCustomization` (`state.ts:804`, `1057`)

The tell that this is one representation too many is that the protocol doc comment has to *teach a rule you must memorize*:

> the **effective** enabled state of a plugin child is the plugin's derived enabled value and `(child.enabled ?? true)`, so a disabled plugin disables every child regardless of each child's own flag. A directory child instead uses the directory's `enabled` value and its own flag.

Two different cascade rules depending on container type, neither enforced anywhere.

Predictably, consumers hand-roll the cascade. The same expression appears in at least three places across two files:

```ts
enabled: isCustomizationEnabled(server) && (!plugin || isCustomizationEnabled(plugin))
```

- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostCustomizationService.ts:191`
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostCustomizationService.ts:218`
- `src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts:3691`

There are ~32 enablement-derivation sites in total across the agent host and its consumers. Any one of them getting the cascade subtly wrong is a silently-wrong enabled state in the UI or, worse, at the SDK boundary.

## Suggestions

**Minimum viable:** export a single `isEffectivelyEnabled(child, container)` in `common/customizationEnablement.ts` and use it everywhere the cascade is currently re-derived. Cheap, no protocol change, removes the duplication.

**Better, if a protocol change is acceptable:** collapse to one representation so directories and plugins cascade identically and the doc comment no longer needs to describe two rules. Note the protocol lives in [microsoft/agent-host-protocol](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol) (`types/` is canonical; vscode's `common/state/protocol/` mirrors it), so this needs a change there first.

title: agent host: derive MCP customization id from ownership instead of publication position

labels.name: debt
labels.description: Code quality issues

labels.name: agent-host
labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

body:
Follow-up cleanup from the scoped-enablement work (#330566, #330715).

## Problem

An MCP server currently carries three identifiers, and most of the hard bugs in this area were *mapping errors between them*:

| Identifier | Value | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `mcp-top-level:<provider>:<session>:<name>` **or** the plugin child id | publication position |
| `name` | server name | SDK operations |
| durable enablement key | `<owningPluginSource>#mcp=<name>` or `mcpServers#<name>` | ownership |

Publication position is decided by a startup race in `McpCustomizationController._applyOne`: if a plugin's children are already published the server is nested, otherwise it is **promoted** to a bare top-level customization, and promotion is deliberately sticky because re-parenting mid-session would orphan an id the client has already rendered.

Because position leaked into identity, the same server keyed differently depending on whether it happened to be promoted that session — so "disable azure globally" written in one session was invisible in the next. That was the original reported bug.

It is currently fixed by threading an ownership map (`mcpServerOwners` / `pluginMcpServerSources`) so the durable key is position-independent. That works, but it means correctness now *depends on every provider remembering to supply the map* — and Codex did not, which is #330715.

## Suggestion

Mint the top-level customization id **from the durable key** rather than from provider/session/name. Then:

- nested and promoted publications are the same identity **by construction**;
- the ownership map stops being load-bearing for correctness and is only needed for display grouping;
- sticky promotion stops being an invariant contributors must preserve;
- the whole "should we gate publication on plugin parsing?" question becomes a pure UX decision rather than a correctness one.

Higher risk than the other follow-ups because it touches id minting, which clients render — worth checking whether any client persists these ids. But it deletes the bug class rather than guarding it.

## Constraint

`getCustomizationEnablementKey` output must not change for existing keys, or users' stored decisions silently orphan and disabled servers come back enabled.

body:
Follow-up cleanup from the scoped-enablement work (#330566, #330715).

## Problem

`resolveCustomizationEnablement` in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/shared/customizationEnablementGate.ts` now takes six parameters, the last three of which are all optional and all different views of the same client state:

```ts
export function resolveCustomizationEnablement(
	service: IAgentHostCustomizationEnablementService,
	session: URI,
	customizations: readonly Customization[],
	clientChildEnablement?: ReadonlyMap<string, Readonly<Record<string, readonly CustomizationEnablement[]>>>,
	clientPlugins?: ReadonlyMap<string, ClientPluginCustomization>,
	mcpServerOwners?: ReadonlyMap<string, string>,
): IResolvedCustomizationEnablement
```

There are 14 call sites across 5 files, and because every extra argument is optional, **omitting one is silent**. That is not hypothetical:

- Codex never supplied the ownership map to its `McpCustomizationController`, so a promoted plugin-owned MCP server keyed as `mcpServers#<name>` instead of `<plugin>#mcp=<name>` and forgot its global/workspace decision across sessions. Fixed in #330715, but only after it was found by hand.
- Auditing whether a given omission is a bug is genuinely hard. Codex's two `resolveCustomizationEnablement` call sites still omit `mcpServerOwners`, and that is *fine* — they only pass plugin candidates, so the nested branch derives ownership from the plugin in hand. But establishing that took several minutes of tracing. A reviewer cannot tell by looking.

## Suggestion

Collapse the three client-state parameters into a single explicit context object, e.g.

```ts
interface ICustomizationResolutionContext {
	readonly clientChildEnablement?: ...;
	readonly clientPlugins?: ...;
	readonly mcpServerOwners?: ...;
}
```

Even keeping the members optional, a named object gives one documented place describing what a caller is expected to provide and why, and makes "which views of client state does this call site have?" reviewable at a glance. Better still if the shape can be made required-with-explicit-empty, so forgetting one is a type error.

Low risk, mechanical, and it would have made the Codex gap impossible to introduce.

title: agent host: make customization resolution unskippable at publication

labels.name: debt
labels.description: Code quality issues

labels.name: agent-host

body:
Follow-up cleanup from the scoped-enablement work (#330566, #330715).

## Problem

Three of the six production bugs found while building scoped enablement had the same shape: a code path emitted a customization **without resolving its enablement first**. The offending sites were four in `copilotAgent`, one in `mcpCustomizationController`, and the post-startup MCP reconcile.

Each was fixed individually, and the invariant was written down — *every publication path must go through `resolveCustomizationEnablement`* — including in the [`customizations-in-the-agent-host` skill](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/.github/skills/customizations-in-the-agent-host/SKILL.md). But an invariant enforced by discipline is one the next contributor can violate silently, and the failure mode is bad: a customization published with stale or absent enablement means a server the user disabled still reaches the model.

## Suggestion

Make it structurally impossible rather than a documented rule. Have the emit/publish helper accept *unresolved* customizations and resolve internally, so there is no way to call it with unresolved state. Callers stop choosing whether to resolve.

This converts a recurring bug class into a compile-time impossibility. Of the simplifications spun out of this work, it has the best value-to-risk ratio.

## Notes

- Watch the pending path: resolution can legitimately return a `pending` result, and SDK-boundary consumers must keep failing closed via `isCustomizationSdkEligible`. Pending must stay *transient* — a cached pending verdict silently drops a customization forever (a separate bug fixed in #330566).
- The regression guard to keep meaningful is the gate test asserting that a server published top-level and the same server published nested resolve to the same durable decision (`customizationEnablementGate.test.ts`).

title: agentHost: anchor the side chat boundary to the inherited turn id
body:
Supersedes #330905, which this branch contains in full.

## The defect

A side chat forks its source chat, so its transcript starts with inherited turns
and continues with its own turns. The boundary was kept only as a turn count in
the persisted backing. The count is a copy of a value that changes with time, and
a recompute in `createChat` wrote the full transcript length back into it. When
that recompute ran again for a chat that already had its own turns, the count
increased and the display hid the turns of the user. In one session the count
moved from 16 to 24 and hid 8 turns.

## The fix

The last turn a side chat inherits is now recorded by id, as `inheritedTurnId`.
A fork copies the transcript, so that id carries over unchanged and names a turn
of the very list the reads slice. It stays correct while the chat grows, and it
tells the seed marker of the chat apart from the markers of the side chats it
descends from.

The boundary resolves in this order:

1. `inheritedTurnId`, when the transcript still holds that turn.
2. The last `<side-chat-context>` seed marker, which repairs a chat whose
   recorded value drifted.
3. `inheritedTurnCount`, for a chat that an older build wrote.

- Removes the recompute in `createChat` that wrote the transcript length into
  `inheritedTurnCount`. The value from the fork is correct and must stay.
- Adds `sliceSideChatTurns`, which resolves the boundary, slices, strips the seed
  and reports a misalignment to the log. The Copilot and Claude read paths use it.
- Compares against the resolved boundary in `prepareSideChatPrompt`, so a value
  that is too large can no longer cause a second seed injection.
- Adds a warning when a fork does not find its anchor turn. The fallback treats
  the full source as inherited, which hid all turns without a record.
- Extracts the seed parser from `stripSideChatContext` so that detection and
  removal of the seed cannot diverge.
- Binds two side chat test fakes to the sends of the recorder instead of a count
  of `getMessages` calls. The count made the tests depend on the defect.

Chats that an older build wrote need no migration, because the repair occurs at
read time.

## Note on the previous revision

#330905 resolved the boundary from the last seed marker alone. Copilot reported
that this breaks a side chat that forks another side chat: before the child sends
anything, the only marker it holds is the one of the parent. The report was
correct, and a test now covers that case together with the case after the first
message.

title: Extension command titles lose localization after installing/updating an extension until full restart (VS Code 1.133)
body:
**Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?:** No - the issue affects ALL extensions' command titles when a language pack is active.

**Issue:**
After installing or updating ANY extension while VS Code is running, all extension command titles in the Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) lose their localization (revert to English), even though the built-in commands remain localized. The issue persists until VS Code is **fully restarted** (File > Exit, not Reload Window). Switching profiles (which triggers a full extension re-scan) also temporarily restores localization.

**Environment:**
- VS Code Version: 1.133.0
- OS Version: Windows
- Language pack: Chinese (Simplified) 1.131.2026072717 (ms-ceintl.vscode-language-pack-zh-hans)
- Profiles in use: custom profiles (Base, Base->Dev) with inherit-profile-plus

**Steps to Reproduce:**
1. Start VS Code with a language pack active (e.g. Chinese). Extension commands are localized correctly.
2. Install or update ANY third-party extension (e.g. via `code --install-extension <vsix>` or the Extensions view).
3. Open Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P). Now ALL third-party extension command titles show in English (e.g. "TokenRhythm: Manage API Keys" instead of the Chinese "管理 API Keys"). Other extensions (GitLens, Python, etc.) are affected too.
4. Reload Window (Developer: Reload Window) does NOT fix it.
5. Fully exit VS Code and restart -> localization returns.

**Expected:** Extension command titles remain localized after extension install/update without a full restart.

**Actual:** Extension command titles revert to English until full restart.

**Additional evidence:**
- Built-in (core) command titles remain localized - only extension-provided commands lose translations.
- Exthost log shows repeated warnings after the install: `Using default string since no string found in i18n bundle that has the key: ...` (e.g. from the built-in Copilot extension).
- The extension's own `package.nls.zh-cn.json` file is intact (valid JSON, UTF-8, no BOM) and present in the installed extension folder and inside the .vsix.
- Language pack caches are intact: `%APPDATA%\Code\languagepacks.json` and `%APPDATA%\Code\clp\<hash>.zh-cn\tcf.json` both exist with correct mappings.
- Root-cause hypothesis: the extension scanner (`extensionsScannerService`) uses the correct `zh-cn` locale during a full scan (startup / profile switch), but during the **incremental re-scan** triggered by an extension install/update, `nlsConfiguration.language` is missing, so `package.nls.<locale>.json` is never loaded for the updated extension and the manifest `%key%` references are not translated.

title: fix(search): support GB2312/GBK encoding in workspace text search (fix #327568)
body:
Fixes #327568

### Description of Changes
When searching workspace text files saved under legacy or alternate encodings (e.g., Simplified Chinese \GB2312\ / \GBK\), \NativeTextSearchManager\ and \ipgrepTextSearchEngine\ map settings \ iles.encoding\ via \	oCanonicalName\. Previously, \	oCanonicalName('gb2312')\ returned \gb2312\ unmapped, which caused ripgrep or standard WHATWG encoding resolvers to fail decoding GBK/GB2312 workspace files on disk unless the file was already opened in an editor tab.

This PR updates \	oCanonicalName\ in \ncoding.ts\ to map \gb2312\ to canonical \gbk\, ensuring disk search correctly parses GB2312/GBK files matching opened buffer search behavior.

### Testing
- Added unit test in \	extSearchManager.test.ts\ verifying \gb2312\ maps to canonical \gbk\ in \NativeTextSearchManager\.

title: fix(terminal): prevent canvas flickering during resize (fix #328100)
body:
Fixes #328100

### Description of Changes
During terminal panel drag-resizing, \TerminalResizeDebouncer\ previously updated vertical rows (\_resizeYCallback\) synchronously per frame while debouncing horizontal columns (\_debounceResizeXScheduler\) for 100ms. Because the container DOM element (\.terminal-wrapper\) expands/shrinks immediately, this caused xterm's WebGL canvas and DOM layout elements to operate with mismatched dimensions (\staleCols\ vs \
ewRows\) for 100ms while dragging, resulting in canvas stretching, reflow jumps, and visual flickering.

This PR updates \TerminalResizeDebouncer\ to synchronize column and row updates atomically (\_resizeBothCallback\) when debouncing X/Y dimension updates, ensuring xterm resizes both dimensions together without intermediate mismatched state.

### Testing
- Added unit tests in \	erminalResizeDebouncer.test.ts\ to verify atomic dimension updates during immediate and debounced resize passes.
